label: Choice-cell determination laws, from the definitions
meaning: Law 1 is the definition of Cstit read as cell-range exclusion. Law 2 is set algebra, using that the cell range lies in the realized range. Law 3: with one cell, Cstit of 'not y' quantifies over every history. Law 4: with one cell, selection says every history has the actual outcome. Law 5 uses excluded middle on the outcome of a cell member. Law 6: a history with another outcome lies outside the selecting cell, so the cell proposition is not necessary, and a single-cell level's cell contains that history. Law 7 transports Cstit along equal cells. Law 8 applies law 6 to an outcome-fine cell. Laws 1, 5 and 7 are near-definitional; laws 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 have short proofs.
